time_source.rule: the lease is issued, opened, authorized, checked and closed at the instant of the supplied hb_epoch on the HB32 lattice; nothing reads a clock
time_source.epoch_rule: org-kernel/kernel.py::supplied_epoch_failure (ASCII [0-9]+, value >= 32; derived_from_clock must be exactly false)
time_source.instant_unix_seconds: instant_unix_ns / 1e9 (float), for consumers whose lease expiry is unix seconds
time_source.expires_at: the issuing instant plus lease_seconds (1..900), on the same lattice

implementations.StegVerse-Labs/StegApp: consumer: stegapp/eia_runtime.invoke(clock=...) receives a supplied-epoch clock built to this contract; a wall clock is not a conforming clock

invariants: no clock read in the lease path; a process that bound lease_time cannot reach the vendored datetime.now fallback
one lease contract: any other browser lease in the ecosystem binds this file by sha256 rather than restating the rule
every refusal terminates FAIL_CLOSED with the six fields; no step waits on an LLM or a person
